newsitem.title: USA: N.J. school districts reject merger plan -- paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. school districts reject merger plan -- paper.

text.p: Voters in Hasbrouck Heights and Wood-Ridge, N.J., on Tuesday defeated a plan to merge the two school districts, the Bergen Record reported Wednesday.
Hasbrouck Heights voters turned down the idea, but residents in Wood-Ridge, the smaller of the two districts, voted overwhelmingly in favor. Both had to approve for the plan to be implemented.
Hasbrouck Heights Superintendent Howard Herbert said the defeat means the district will have to pay to expand, rather than use the under-utilized facilities in Wood-Ridge.
Herbert said the district would have to ask voters to approve at least a $9 million building and renovation bond proposal.
